notes: Access: direct fetch worked throughout, no blocking encountered. Site is Next.js/GraphQL (M&S 'productPageData.search.results'); each category page embeds a __NEXT_DATA__ JSON blob with results.totalItems and a matching rendered 'N Items' header text -- used both together as the qty evidence (they agreed on every row checked). Verified totalItems is NOT the Categories-facet count read from a parent page: on the parent Home Accessories and Lighting/Tableware listing pages the 'Categories' facet gave counts that differed by a few units from the child page's own totalItems (e.g. Vases 62 on facet vs 57 direct; Photo Frames 62 vs 61; Lamp Shades 40 vs 44; Wall Lights 30 vs 31; Glassware 117 vs 111; Mugs 103 vs 104) -- per Rule 1 (counts can drift / facet indexes can be stale) every qty in this file is the number read directly off that subcategory's own URL, confirmed against its own rendered header text, not copied from a parent facet. Additionally did a pagination exhaustion check on Wall Art (333 items): page 7 (last full page) returned exactly 45 tiles (288+45=333) and page 8 redirected back to page 1 (no such page), confirming 333 is exact and not inflated. Full Home Accessories facet breakdown (848 total) summed exactly to its parent totalItems, corroborating the facet mechanism is basically sound, just occasionally a few items stale versus the live child page -- child page value was always preferred. Home site nav ('Home' top-level) is /c/home-and-furniture, covering Bedding, Furniture, Home Furnishings, Bathroom, Lighting, Tableware, Kitchenware, Home Accessories -- all fully explored via each section's own __NEXT_DATA__ facets. Excluded entirely as non-decor: Bedding (textiles), Furniture (all types), Home Furnishings (cushions/curtains/rugs/throws -- textiles), Bathroom Towels/Bath&Shower Mats (textiles/functional) and the single-item 'Bathroom Accessories' node (qty 1, no usable product name, too small/ambiguous to be a real category), all of Kitchenware (Pots & Pans, Kitchen Utensils, Kitchen Storage, Baking, Travel Mugs, Lunch Boxes, Kitchen Textiles, Dish Racks -- all functional cookware/storage, no decor line found). Under Home Accessories excluded: Home Fragrance/Candles (92 items, titles sampled -- 'Restore 3 Wick Candle', 'Calm Box Candle', 'Meadow Floral Scented Candle' etc, overwhelmingly scented, dropped whole Candles node per Home Fragrance rule) and Home Fragrance/Diffusers/Room Spray/Gift sets (all fragrance); kept Home Fragrance/Candle Holders (35, unscented decorative holders, titles sampled e.g. 'Marble Hurricane Candle Holder' -- confirmed non-fragranced); also excluded Artificial Flowers (61, faux plants rule), Storage (20, functional storage boxes/baskets, not decor) and Books (15, not decor). Under Tableware excluded Table Linen (52, textile) and Cutlery (6, flatware, explicitly excluded); kept Teapots & Cafetieres (21) under Kitchen & Dining per this project's established precedent (multiple prior companies in this run filed teapots there). Photo Frames kept under Home Accessories per this project's established precedent across many prior companies (Wall Decor & Mirrors / Home Accessories -> Picture/Photo Frames rows exist in c1-c90). No dedicated Clocks category exists anywhere in the Home Accessories/Home-and-Furniture tree (checked the exhaustive Categories facet which sums exactly to the parent total, and tried a direct /clocks URL guess -- 404); this is a legitimate absence, not an oversight. Lighting: verified every branch present (Table Lamps, Ceiling Lights, Lamp Shades, Floor Lamps, Wall Lights, Outdoor Lights, String Lights); excluded Lightbulbs (5, bulbs explicitly excluded). No 'Lighting by Room' room-branch nav exists on M&S (flat fixture-type taxonomy only, no Bathroom/Bedroom/Outdoor lighting sub-nodes beyond the single flat 'Outdoor Lights' node, which is included as a fixture-type branch, not a room re-cut). No separate room-based Mirrors nav either (single flat Mirrors category, 87 items) -- so Rule 0's room-vs-type distinction did not surface any additional rows to include beyond the flat taxonomy already covered; the one place it mattered was confirming Outdoor Lights (2) stays IN because it is a legitimate fixture-type/location node, not excluded as 'outdoor'. No Rule 0.6 overlap situations found -- M&S's taxonomy is a single flat type-tree with no parallel room-tree, so no duplicate-population rows were dropped or merged.
